paper: Hubble: An LLM-Driven Agentic Framework for Safe, Diverse, and Reproducible Alpha Factor Discovery
claim_boundary: A researcher-authored monthly U.S.-stock analogue of Hubble's safe DSL/AST candidate generation, positive/negative retrieval guidance, three-round feedback, standardized multi-metric evaluation, similarity and crowding penalties, and family-capped top-five selection; not the intentionally withheld formulas or native LLM run.

paper_source.bounded_release_search_checked_2026_09_0: Exact-title, arXiv-ID, author, and lab searches expose the paper and summaries but no attributable runtime, operator registry, candidate records, or top-five formulas.

primary_source_anchors.mechanism: A constrained DSL and three-layer AST sandbox restrict candidates to safe interpretable operator trees while positive RAG encourages under-covered mechanisms and negative RAG discourages crowded templates.
Every valid candidate receives RankIC, Pearson IC, long-short return, turnover, coverage, and AST complexity diagnostics under one deterministic evaluation pipeline.
Standardized metrics are combined with crowded-template, similarity, family-concentration, and novelty adjustments; top factors and family diagnostics persist into later rounds.
The main run uses three rounds and top-k five with at most two factors per family; the selected families are two range, two volatility, and one trend, but exact formulas are withheld.

safe_search_policy.feedback_rule: each later round excludes exact prior candidates and rewards families absent from the current selected set
safe_search_policy.missing_factor_value_rule: replace a missing selected factor rank with cross-sectional neutral zero after coverage has been penalized during selection
safe_search_policy.final_score: equal mean of the five validation-oriented selected factor ranks
safe_search_policy.common_portfolio_adapter: the frozen top-five score enters value-weighted long-short deciles and all six common cost/missing-return paths

preserved_elements: AST structural, complexity, and semantic validation
deterministic RankIC and Pearson IC evaluation
long-short return, turnover, coverage, and complexity diagnostics
approximated_elements: JKP technical characteristics replace raw daily OHLCV
five transparent operations replace the private operator registry
family exemplars replace positive RAG documents
a liquidity-volume family penalty replaces negative RAG retrieval
pre-common 1989-1999 evaluation replaces the native discovery slice
cross-candidate z/tanh standardization replaces undisclosed centers and scales
equal selected-factor aggregation replaces absent formulas and portfolio rules
invented_elements: the candidate enumeration order and per-round partition
AST depth four and seven-node caps
